heroHeadline: Magyar Inaugurated as PM on Europe Day; EU Flag Restored; Sulyok Given May 31 Deadline
heroSubtitle: Péter Magyar was sworn in as Prime Minister of Hungary on May 9, 2026 — Europe Day — with 140 parliamentary votes, ending 16 years of Orbán rule. Speaker Ágnes Forsthoffer's first act was restoring the EU flag to parliament after ~12 years' absence. Magyar demanded President Sulyok resign by May 31. First decrees established an anti-corruption office and submitted Hungary's EPPO membership application. The forint hit near four-year highs as EU fund reform milestones are due end of May.
footerNote: Tracker covers Hungary's political transition from Orbán's 2010 return to power through the 2026 post-election transition. Data reflects publicly available reports from verified sources.
